summary: Iteration 1 validated that directed Pósa rotations are the dominant algorithmic improvement for the Hamiltonian Path problem, lifting the score from 41 (greedy only) to 72 (greedy + rotation). The algorithm now solves 7 of 10 test cases perfectly but fails on the 3 hardest cases (tests 4, 8, 10) which have sparser graphs with many low-degree vertices. The next iteration should focus on closing the 28-point gap on those hard cases.
key_points: SCORE 72 achieved (up from 41 baseline). Pósa rotation enables full Hamiltonian path discovery on 7/10 tests by escaping dead ends via O(1) linked-list path restructuring. The 31-point gap between rotation and no-rotation is decisive and reproducible.

Three hard tests remain unsolved: test 4 (n=500, k=223/500, 1/10 pts), test 8 (n=9000, k=3309/9000, 1/10 pts), and test 10 (n=100K, k=4966/100K, 0/10 pts). These share low average degree (~3) and high proportions of low-degree vertices (16-41%), making rotation shortcuts rare.

Key failed approaches: backward Pósa rotations (scored 64-65 vs 72 forward-only, likely a bug), DFS with backtracking (scored 33), ruin-and-recreate local search (scored 40), multi-seed strategies (seed-sensitive, 55-72 depending on time allocation).

Next iteration should investigate: (1) debugging backward rotations to potentially double the escape options at dead ends, (2) SCC-aware or topological construction for sparse graphs, (3) more aggressive multi-restart strategies with better seed selection, and (4) test-case-adaptive time budgets that allocate more time to hard instances. Fixing backward rotations alone could unlock tests 4 and 8 (worth up to 18 more points).
